description: Remove overly generic terms from CODING_PATTERNS that cause false-positive coding model selection for monitoring tasks
rationale: The Proctor is a monitoring/observability bot — terms like 'log', 'error', 'api', 'database', 'query', 'service', 'test', and 'thread' appear in almost every monitoring request. These generic terms cause is_coding_task() to return True for routine monitoring queries, unnecessarily switching to the coding model and adding latency. Removing them keeps coding detection accurate for actual code-editing tasks.

description: Increase LLM_MAX_TOKENS default to reduce truncation risk for complex observability analysis
rationale: The Proctor specializes in log analysis, metrics collection, and incident detection — tasks that often produce detailed, lengthy responses. With 4096 max tokens, complex log analysis or multi-service health reports may get truncated, requiring follow-up calls that increase total latency (currently 22.2s avg). Doubling the token limit allows the model to complete analysis in a single call.
new_code_preview: LLM_MAX_TOKENS = _llm.get("max_tokens", 8192)

description: Reduce LLM timeout from 120s to 90s for faster failure on hung requests
rationale: Average LLM latency is 27.23s. A 120s timeout means a hung request blocks the bot for 2 full minutes before failing. 90s still provides ample headroom (3.3x the average) while failing 25% faster on stuck requests, improving error recovery and user experience.
new_code_preview: LLM_TIMEOUT = 90

description: Reduce session history token budget from 1536 to 1024 to offset 194-tool context bloat
rationale: With 194 MCP tools in the context, tool definitions alone consume a massive portion of the context window. Reducing session history from 1536 to 1024 tokens frees ~512 tokens for tool definitions and memory injection without losing meaningful conversation continuity. This directly addresses the 27s latency by reducing total input token count.
old_code_preview: SESSION_HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS = 1536  # Reserve ~37% of context for session history, leaving more for tool outputs and memory
new_code_preview: SESSION_HISTORY_MAX_TOKENS = 1024  # Reduced from 1536: 194 MCP tool definitions consume significant context; 1024 tokens (~25%) still preserves recent conversation continuity

description: Reduce LLM max output tokens from 4096 to 2048 for faster response generation
rationale: For a Discord chat bot with a nautical persona, 4096 output tokens is excessive — most responses are a few paragraphs. Halving to 2048 reduces generation time significantly (output token count is the primary driver of LLM latency), directly addressing the 27s average latency. The voice prompt already asks for 2-4 sentences, and text responses rarely need more than 2048 tokens.
new_code_preview: LLM_MAX_TOKENS = 2048

description: Add tool selection guidance to system prompt MCP section to reduce LLM cognitive load
rationale: With 194 tools, the LLM may waste inference time scanning all tool definitions. Explicitly instructing it to first identify the relevant server namespace, then select tools only from that server, reduces the decision space and should improve both latency and tool selection accuracy. This is a zero-risk prompt change that guides the LLM's attention.
old_code_preview: These tools are discovered dynamically. Use them when the task requires external service access.
new_code_preview: These tools are discovered dynamically. You have nearly 200 tools available — do NOT scan or reason through all of them. Instead, identify the relevant server (github, gmail_freelance, schubert, postg

description: Reduce MCP tool retry initial delay from 1.0s to 0.5s for faster recovery
rationale: With exponential backoff, the initial delay of 1.0s means 3 retries take 1+2+4=7s. Reducing to 0.5s makes 3 retries take 0.5+1+2=3.5s, cutting retry overhead by 50% while still providing backoff. This improves recovery speed when MCP servers have transient connection issues without increasing load.
new_code_preview: MCP_TOOL_RETRY_DELAY = 0.5  # seconds, exponential backoff (reduced from 1.0 for faster transient failure recovery)

description: Reduce LLM_TIMEOUT from 90s to 60s — avg latency is 25.4s, so 60s provides ample margin while failing faster on hung requests
rationale: With avg_llm_latency_s of 25.4s, a 90s timeout is overly generous. Hung requests waste the Captain's time for 90s before failing. 60s gives 2.3x the average latency as margin, which is sufficient. The 1 LLM error in the last 7 days may have been a timeout that could have recovered faster.
new_code_preview: LLM_TIMEOUT = 60

description: Reduce AGENT_TIMEOUT from 300s to 180s — 5 minutes is excessive for a single agent loop iteration
rationale: A 5-minute agent timeout means the Captain could wait 5 minutes before a single agent loop fails. With 25.4s avg LLM latency and MAX_ITERATIONS=30, most agent loops should complete well under 3 minutes. 180s still allows complex multi-tool investigations while preventing indefinite hangs.
new_code_preview: AGENT_TIMEOUT = 180

rationale: With 194 MCP tool definitions consuming substantial context tokens, and the verbose system prompt, 1024 tokens for session history is still too generous. 768 tokens (~4-6 exchanges) is sufficient for conversation continuity while freeing ~256 tokens for memory injection and tool output.

description: Add stale user cleanup to rate limiter to prevent memory leak
rationale: The _command_timestamps dict accumulates entries for every user who ever sends a command, never removing inactive users. Over weeks/months in long-running channels, this grows unboundedly. Adding a size-based cleanup prevents the memory leak identified in optimization priority #6.

description: Reduce LLM_TIMEOUT from 60s to 45s for faster failure detection
rationale: Average LLM latency is 23.01s. A 45s timeout provides ~2x headroom over average while failing hung requests 15s sooner, reducing user wait time on stuck calls. The single error in 312 calls (0.3% error rate) suggests timeouts are rare, so 45s is safe.
new_code_preview: LLM_TIMEOUT = 45

description: Reduce AGENT_TIMEOUT from 180s to 120s
rationale: A 3-minute agent timeout is excessive. With 0 agent requests in 7 days, the agent loop is rarely used. 120s (2 minutes) is sufficient for multi-step tool chains while preventing long-running stuck agents from consuming resources.
new_code_preview: AGENT_TIMEOUT = 120

description: Reduce SHELL_TIMEOUT from 120s to 90s
rationale: Most shell commands (systemctl, git, log viewing) complete in under 10s. A 90s timeout still allows for longer operations like git clones or large file processing while failing truly hung commands 30s sooner.
new_code_preview: SHELL_TIMEOUT = 90

description: Improve rate limit cleanup to remove only stale users instead of clearing all
rationale: The current approach clears ALL rate limit data when the dict exceeds 1000 entries, which resets rate limits for active users and could allow burst violations. Selectively removing only stale users (no activity in 60s) preserves rate limiting for active users while preventing unbounded dict growth.
